criteria.accept_quiet_window: Ratify the artifact as built: fixed 5s mail deadline per delivery, 8 phases, 30+ toolchain-booted sender runs. Record the quiet-machine operating requirement (load circa 35-40 or below), run its F01 rerun in isolation, and live with red runs whenever parallel workers saturate the host. Zero further implementation; the obligation stands on documented conditions.
criteria.patient_timeouts: Lengthen the mail-phase waiting budget toward the 30s the Python baseline allowed each phase group, without touching any verdict: deliveries stay real, staged, and mailbox-judged through the production Can sender. Re-verify live once after retiming and proceed through the normal gates. Spends one more worker loop; both retired .py files remain retired.

a02_durability.instructions: Which treatment of the timing-fragile A02 probe keeps its obligation genuine while staying honest about what the clock measures?

state.durability_stakes: F01 must re-execute each retired port on demand, and progress counts only fulfilled baseline obligations. An artifact that greens only on an idle host is a brittle promise: any later rerun under normal parallel load goes red for environmental reasons. The 256 GB laptop routinely sits at load 40-60+ with three workers; sub-40 windows exist only beside at most one quiet task.
state.load_evidence: Green evidence is the worker's 38-minute rc=0 (27 checks) beside its own measurement of roughly 7.6 CPU-s per delivery against a hard 5s mail deadline, workable only near or below load 35-40. Coordinator reruns at load 60+ produced two code 10 stage failures and one code 20 spawn failure at 43m34s. The 124/124 build is load-independent and confirmed by both parties.
state.mandate: The language is written by AI agents and owes nothing to prior artifacts; project law ranks goal attainment over scaffolding and proof layering. Both signup harnesses (tests/auth_signup/probe.py, tests/auth_signup/fake_mail.py) already retired at 5ec1cdb in favor of tests/auth_signup/probe/. The choice is between reworking that living probe and formally accepting its envelope.
state.production_timing: Real deliveries complete in well under a second; the baseline's 30s per-phase-group budget was headroom that never engaged. The observed 7.6 CPU-s per delivery is the Can toolchain starting up inside every `canlc run` sender call, not mail latency in production. Hence the 5s probe deadline meters harness boot rather than the property judged (a genuine delivery reaching the mailbox), which carries no timing term.
state.worker_record: Ten commits show real iteration against observed behavior: empty-grandchild environment handling, expiry tolerance, splitting P1 into single-delivery driver runs. The worker surfaced the load limit itself and both refusal controls fire. Good faith is not in doubt; the undecided point is whether the accepted probe is durable enough to hold the record.
